name: default

category.instructions: Classify this email into exactly ONE category by its NATURE — what kind of communication it is, not how important it feels. When several apply, take the earliest in this order: security, spam, finance, notifications, marketing, action, work. Internal colleague mail is categorized exactly like external mail. Any language; judge meaning, never words.

criteria.security: ACCOUNT-SECURITY events and threats: sign-in alerts, verification codes, password resets, MFA challenges, alerts about suspicious activity, and impersonation/phishing attempts. Evidence: the message concerns access to an account, or shows deception indicators. Note: 'security' describes what the mail is ABOUT; how likely it is to be a real threat is the separate suspicious judgment. A legitimate code from the real service is security with low suspicion.
criteria.spam: Unsolicited junk or bulk mail with no legitimate connection to the mailbox owner: generic promotions to a list, scams, chain letters. Evidence: no real relationship, no work context, mass-mailing nature.
criteria.finance: MONEY matters: invoices, payments, receipts, banking, billing, quotes, budgets, subscriptions, expenses, taxes, payroll. Evidence: amounts, payment instructions, or billing language.
criteria.notifications: AUTOMATED machine mail: alerts, digests, monitoring, CI/CD, build results, shipping updates, social-network activity, forum replies, webhooks. Evidence: system sender, generated content, no human sign-off — even when it asks for a click, it is still a notification, never action.
criteria.marketing: COMMERCIAL promotion: product announcements, newsletters, deals, webinar invitations, ads, press releases. Evidence: selling or promoting to an audience, not corresponding about work.
criteria.action: A HUMAN BEING explicitly asks the mailbox owner for something concrete: a reply to a question, a file, a decision, an approval, a task, a meeting, a payment. Evidence: an explicit ask directed at the owner in the text — without such an ask this category does not apply. Automated mail is never action regardless of what it requests.
criteria.work: HUMAN work correspondence that informs, updates, or coordinates without asking anything of the owner: status updates, threads, logistics, schedules, reports, receipts of process, thank-yous.

topic.instructions: What is this email about? Pick the single topic that best matches its request or content, regardless of language.

criteria.project_work: Ongoing projects, deliverables, tasks, and status of work.
criteria.support_issue: Problems, bug reports, incidents, troubleshooting, help requests.
criteria.sales_inquiry: Buying, selling, quotes, pricing, and commercial negotiation.
criteria.technical_integration: APIs, software setup, integrations, credentials, configuration.
criteria.internal_ops: Company-internal operations, HR, policies, tools, administration.
criteria.news_updates: Newsletters, product updates, industry news, announcements.
criteria.other: Anything that fits none of the topics above.

reply_needed.instructions: Was a query directed at the mailbox owner present in this message when it arrived? Judge only what the message itself asks — whether it has since been handled is not knowable from the text and must not be guessed.

criteria.true: A query directed at the mailbox owner is present: a question aimed at them, or a direct request for information/confirmation that only they can give. Evidence: an interrogative sentence addressed to them, or an explicit ask to come back with an answer. Language is irrelevant; judge meaning.
criteria.false: No query is directed at the owner: pure FYI, acknowledgments, automated mail, the sender answering their own question, questions aimed at someone else, or a request that needs an action (send/approve/pay) rather than an answer.

urgency.instructions: How time-sensitive did the SENDER frame this as, at the moment the mail was sent? Judge the pressure the text expresses relative to the mail's own date — never relative to today, and never from your own guess of importance.
criteria: No time pressure stated or implied - whenever.
Soft preference for speed - soon, when you can, this week if possible.
A concrete near deadline - by Friday, tomorrow, end of week, before a named meeting that is days away.
Explicitly urgent - urgent, ASAP, today, needed before end of day, a same-day meeting or deadline.
Immediate and blocking - emergency, system down, everything is stopped, deadline is right now or already past when the mail was sent.

suspicious.instructions: Does this message show signs of being a phishing attempt, scam, or spoofed sender? Base the verdict only on deception indicators visible in the message — not on unfamiliarity.

criteria.true: Deception indicators are present: a spoofed or look-alike sender, credential or payment redirection, urgency combined with secrecy, an implausible request for money or data, a mismatch between who the mail claims to be and who it actually is, or an attempt to move the conversation to an unusual channel.
criteria.false: The mail reads as genuinely from who it claims to be: ordinary work context, consistent identity, no deception pattern. Unfamiliar sender or commercial tone alone is NOT suspicion — that is marketing or spam's job.

is_question.instructions: Does the TEXT contain questions that expect an answer — regardless of who must answer them? (Whether the answer must come from the mailbox owner specifically is a separate judgment.)

criteria.true: The text contains at least one question that expects an answer from someone. Evidence: an interrogative sentence, or an implicit answer-request ('let me know', 'confirm whether…'). Rhetorical questions the text itself answers do not count.
criteria.false: Statements only, or rhetorical questions answered in the same message.

call_to_action.instructions: Does the message explicitly ask the mailbox owner to DO something concrete — as opposed to answering something? Judge only asks that are directed at them in the text.

criteria.true: An explicit, concrete action is requested of the mailbox owner: send, fix, review, approve, pay, register, attend, click. Evidence: an imperative or a directed request naming the act. Implied or background tasks that the mail only discusses do not count; automated mail never counts.
criteria.false: Nothing concrete is asked of the owner; the mail informs or closes.

decision_needed.instructions: Does the message ask the mailbox owner for a VERDICT — approve/reject, yes/no, choose between options? A decision is a judgment, not a task and not a mere question.

criteria.true: The owner must choose or rule on something to unblock progress: yes/no, approve or reject, pick between options, accept terms. Evidence: the mail explicitly presents a choice or asks for a verdict. A question that merely gathers information is not a decision.
criteria.false: No verdict is being asked for; information or work alone is requested.

asks_for.instructions: What is the sender primarily asking of the mailbox owner? Pick exactly one — the DOMINANT ask, by this precedence when several are present: a decision outranks a task, which outranks a document, which outranks a plain answer; money and time requests rank by what blocks the sender most. If nothing is asked, pick the FYI option.

criteria.answer_question: An answer to a question or a discussion.
criteria.information_document: Information, a document, a file, data, or access.
criteria.task_work: Work to perform: fix, build, review, deliver, follow up.

deadline.instructions: What time frame does the text set for something to happen? Count explicit dates and deadlines AND meetings/events it proposes. Measure the distance from the mail's own date to the named date — a deadline two years ago was once two days away; judge it as the mail framed it.
criteria: No date, deadline, or event is mentioned.
A date far from the mail's own date (months away).
A date within roughly a month of the mail's own date.
A date within roughly a week of the mail's own date.
A date within 24 hours of the mail's own date.
Already overdue at the moment the mail was sent, or due that same day.

relationship.instructions: What is the sender's relationship to the mailbox owner? Judge from the content and the parties involved — internal colleagues, external clients, vendors and automated systems are distinct kinds of relationship. When unclear, pick unknown rather than guessing.

criteria.existing_client: An existing customer or client of the business.
criteria.prospect_lead: A potential customer, lead, or sales contact.
criteria.colleague: A coworker or someone inside the same organization.
criteria.vendor_partner: A supplier, partner, contractor, or service provider.
criteria.automated_service: An automated system, bot, notification, or no-reply service.

effort.instructions: How much work is it for the mailbox owner to handle this message properly? Estimate from what the text actually demands of them — reply length, research, building, coordinating. Judge the work, not the sender's rank or the message's importance.
criteria: None or seconds - nothing to do, or a one-line reply.
Minutes - a short reply, a quick check, a click or a small lookup.
Hours - real work: research, write, review, build, or fix something.
Days - project-level work, coordination of several people, or a deliverable.

sentiment.instructions: What emotional tone does the SENDER express in this message toward the recipient or the situation? Judge the expressed tone only — politeness formulas are neutral.
criteria: Very negative - angry, accusatory, or in conflict
Negative
Neutral
Positive
Very positive

stance.instructions: What does this message primarily do in its conversation? Judge the message itself, whatever side of the exchange it is on.

criteria.asks_questions: Primarily asks questions or requests information.
criteria.provides_answers: Primarily provides answers, information, or an affirmative response.
criteria.both: Both asks and answers/provides in comparable measure.
criteria.acknowledgment: Pure acknowledgment: thanks, receipt confirmation, closing remarks.

info_sufficiency.instructions: Does the message contain everything needed to answer or act on it — context, specifics, links, files, dates — or is something missing that would force a follow-up question back? Evidence: can the needed response be written without inventing or hunting for facts?

criteria.true: Self-contained: everything needed to act is present.
criteria.false: Incomplete: context, specifics, or attachments are missing.

request_count.instructions: How many DISTINCT asks does this message contain? Count by meaning — each separate question, demand, or task counts once; rephrasing the same ask in one message does not make it two.
criteria: None - purely informational
One request
Two requests
Three or more requests

has_signature.instructions: Does the message end with a personal signature block — a name with role, company, phone, address, or other contact details?
